body: Thank you for taking your time to creating an issue for us.  Let me try to fix it in the next stable release.
I made sure the `majorVersion` is either `2` or `3`  everywhere and `3` for SSLv3 and TLSv1.x, so this issue should be fixed now.

Does that resolve the issue of when the Client is using SSL but the server is not?  Making the modification you suggested, that resolved the unresponsiveness when the server was using SSL, but the client was not, but it did not fix it for the inverse; the client still hung waiting for a valid SSL response from the server.

I think it depends on what data the plaintext server sends to the SSL client.  Do you get any exception on the SSL client side?  If so, please paste it here.  If not, it might mean 1) the plaintext server did not send any response or 2) the response the plaintext server sent looked similar to a partial SSL message.  At both cases, you will have to call `Channel.close()` by yourself on read timeout.  If the connection is not closed, please send me the heap dump of the SSL client so that I can check the internal state of the SslHandler to see why the close request is not going through.

I'm just now getting around to this (using Netty 3.5.2) and there is still the issue that the client is not notified that the channel is closed when the server throws an NotSslRecordException.  I am able to see this on the server, and I attach a close listener to the channel after I log the error, but the client never gets the close event, presumably because of the mismatch they cannot communicate?  This makes it very difficult to detect the SSL mismatch if I cannot propagate the error back to the client.

Presumably I could handle this for the most part with a ReadTimeoutHandler, but there are two issues with that.  1) i cant disambiguate b/w an actual timeout and the ssl mismatch so i cannot provide a good error message to the client and 2) the SSL connect will be slower than a normal connect, how do i pick an appropriate timeout for the connections.  what might be reasonable in some environments won't be in others.  i dont think there's a one size fits all timeout.

Any suggestions?
Would you mind if you could provide very simple app that demonstrates the problem?  I want to dig into this a little bit more by myself.

I can more or less get this to happen with the secure chat example.  If I comment out the SSL engine in the client and make the handshake conditional on whether or not there is an SSL handler, no writes to the channel from the client ever gets to the server.  

The connection is successful, i see the that event on the server, but the Greeter never fires.  This is not surprising since there is no handshake that is done, but it means that the server effectively is waiting forever(?) for the handshake to complete

When you type in 'bye' on the client, you get the NotSslRecordException on the server from the client attempting to close the channel.  This latter case is basically what I'm seeing in my app, except the write does seem to go through, and triggers the exception on the server, at which time the server tries to close that connection, but that event never fires.

Similarly, if you disable SSL in the server and make the handshake conditional on the handler, but leave SSL enabled in the client, you can't close the channel on the client afaict; I type in 'bye' and the console just sits there.  Seems like no event can get from the client to the server at all.

I am trying to get these sorts of mismatches to fail gracefully so I can print a reasonable error to the client, that they need to either turn on, or turn off, SSL.
@trustin do you want to have a look at this before 3.5.3.Final ?
I guess the sensible behavior on NotSslRecordException is to close the connection.  Let me just modify SslHandler close the connection automatically.

Please make it configurable and also not enable it by default (at least in 3.x)
